nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: You look terrible, Edmund. Are the children eating?

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: I've been thinking about what you said. About the Ripper detail that didn't fit. I did some digging.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: Spoke to a man at the Met. Off the record. He said the scene was consistent with the previous killings. The constable on duty may have been... overzealous in his report.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: Edmund. You found your wife in an alley at midnight. I am not dismissing what you saw. But grief does extraordinary things to memory.

nodes.speaker: Arthur Crane
nodes.text: That said — Hargrove. Have you spoken to anyone at Whitmore Street yet? I think that's still your best thread.
nodes.journal_entry: Arthur says the police think it matches the Ripper after all. He was so certain, so calm about it. And then he steered me back to Hargrove again.
